# Assets and brand replacement

## Inventory

For every asset record:

- path and original filename;
- width, height, aspect ratio, file size, and alpha channel;
- intended role: brand, product, VI, packaging, scenario, store, screenshot, evidence, or decoration;
- fit mode and focal point;
- source, license, and reuse restriction;
- minimum acceptable rendered size.

## Fit policy

- `contain`: logos, VI sheets, UI screenshots, diagrams, product cutouts, packaging, labels, and any asset whose full boundary is meaningful.
- `cover`: documentary photography only, with an explicit focal point such as `{ "x": 0.63, "y": 0.42 }`.
- Do not crop text, logos, products, or explanatory marks.
- Do not upscale below-minimum imagery. Replace it, use it smaller, or present it as an evidence thumbnail.

## Logo policy

- Prefer transparent PNG, SVG supplied by the user, or a formally approved master.
- If the only logo has a solid background, create a transparent derivative without changing the mark and keep the original.
- Respect safe space and minimum size from the VI guide.

## Brand replacement protocol

Create a replacement table before reuse:

| Source token | Replacement | Scope | Verification |
| --- | --- | --- | --- |
| old brand name | new brand name | visible text, notes, metadata | case-insensitive scan |
| old English name | new English name | visible text, filenames, alt text | case-insensitive scan |
| old logo | approved logo master | images and flattened screenshots | visual review |

Also scan speaker notes, alt text, document properties, captions, filenames, embedded images, and exported PDF text. Flattened old logos require image editing or exclusion; text replacement alone is insufficient.

# Installation and host compatibility · 2.2.0

## Package and runtime

The distribution ZIP has `SKILL.md`, `references/`, `assets/`, `scripts/`, `package.json` and a dependency lockfile at its root. It contains no node_modules, user paths, credentials, fonts or client material.

Unzip into a directory named `leego-design-ppt`. Open a terminal in that directory:

```sh
node scripts/doctor.mjs
npm ci --ignore-scripts
node scripts/validate-deck-spec.mjs --input "/path/to/deck-spec.json"
node scripts/build-web.mjs --input "/path/to/deck-spec.json" --output "/path/to/web"
node scripts/build-pptx.mjs --input "/path/to/deck-spec.json" --output "/path/to/deck.pptx"
node scripts/export-pdf.mjs --input "/path/to/deck.pptx" --output "/path/to/deck.pdf"
```

Use real paths in the host environment, with quotes for spaces/Chinese names. Relative image paths resolve from the spec directory, not the terminal working directory. Node.js 20+ is required. HTML needs no npm packages. PPTX needs the locked `pptxgenjs` and `image-size` packages; npm contacts its configured registry only on explicit installation. PDF needs LibreOffice on PATH, `LIBREOFFICE_PATH`, or `--soffice <executable>`; PowerPoint/WPS manual export is also valid. None of the build scripts installs applications automatically or uploads the input.

## WorkBuddy

Official route: Experts / Skills / Connectors → Skills → Add Skill → Upload Skill. Import the root-entry ZIP, enable it and start a new task. Direct conversation installation is documented for marketplace skills; do not promise a pasted GitHub link installs a custom ZIP.

Ask: “使用 Leego Design PPT。先运行环境检查；按随包说明补齐依赖，再生成三页中文示例并打开检查。保留可编辑文本，图片不变形。没有 PDF 转换器时明确说明，不把网页截图称为可编辑 PPT。”

Source checked 2026-10-25: https://www.codebuddy.cn/docs/workbuddy/From-Beginner-to-Expert-Guide/Function-Description/Skills-Market

## 豆包工作

Use the client’s custom-skill import entry if present, and upload the same ZIP. No verified official universal installation command or filesystem path is assumed. If this account cannot import external skills, attach the ZIP to a file/code-enabled task and request extraction and use of SKILL.md plus its referenced files. That is task-local usage, not permanent installation. A chat-only environment cannot run the scripts; use its native presentation tool according to these design rules and disclose which capabilities are unavailable.

## Capability-based fallback

| Environment | Supported path |
|---|---|
| Can read files only | Use narrative and layout rules with the host’s native output tools; no scripted build claim |
| Node.js 20+, no installed packages | Offline HTML and validation |
| Node.js plus locked npm dependencies | Editable PPTX, HTML |
| Above plus LibreOffice / presentation exporter | PDF from final PPTX |

Passing Node builds on macOS does not establish native WorkBuddy or 豆包 import, Windows execution, font availability, or PowerPoint/WPS visual fidelity. Record each tested surface separately. Run doctor in the actual host before promising output. A missing converter is a visible limitation, not a silent switch to a different document.

If a headless converter substitutes fonts or renders Chinese as boxes, pass `--font-dir "/path/to/licensed/fonts"` to export-pdf.mjs. This sets a temporary fontconfig for that export only. Re-render and inspect actual glyphs; a zero exit status is not proof of usable Chinese text. The directory is not copied into the Skill.

## Updates

2.2+ uses the [live rules channel](live-updates.md). Node/network access is needed to check; offline and restricted hosts keep local guidance. This does not grant universal access to another user's Skill directory.

# Content-driven design decisions

Use for new decks, narrative restructuring or an explicit visual redesign. Preserve approved decks for scoped edits. Read `data/design-library.json` selectively; it contains eight original style families, six scenarios and the 20 existing baseline layouts, not 30 bespoke templates or 20 new visualization engines.

## Decision sequence

1. Extract audience, intended decision, setting (projection or reading), evidence, approved brand, delivery format and page scope. Resolve from the conversation before asking. Do not invent missing business inputs.
2. Choose a scenario and narrative arc. Shareholder review generally moves from operating conclusion to performance evidence, diagnosis and strategic decisions. Brand partnerships need proposition, product/context evidence and cooperation boundaries. Adjust to the real audience.
3. Choose compatible style families, then one coherent deck-wide system. Approved brand constraints take precedence. A data page may combine consulting structure with brand color without randomly changing themes.
4. For each page, identify intent, evidence shape, quantity and readability constraints. Trend → line; magnitude/rank → bar; detailed comparison → table; system layers → architecture; steps → process; real product/screenshot → contain image. Missing values remain missing. Distribution/composition charts require a custom implementation; do not mislabel current bar/line support.
5. Record why the choice fits, what was rejected and what must be split or supplied. `plan-design.mjs` is an explainable baseline selector, not a full aesthetic judge or natural-language author. The agent turns the brief into explicit inputs and applies its reviewed plan to the deck-spec.
6. Build using existing H5/PPTX/PDF tools. Review every changed page. A successful selector test is not proof of visual superiority.

Run from the installed Skill directory:

```sh
node scripts/plan-design.mjs --input /path/to/design-brief.json --output /path/to/design-plan.json
```

Brief shape:

```json
{"audience":"股东","scenario":"shareholder-review","goal":"决定下一年度资源配置","brand":{"approved":false},"delivery":"pptx","slides":[{"id":"trend","intent":"trend","data":{"available":true,"labels":4,"series":1,"hasMissing":false,"unit":"万元","period":"年度","source":"已核实经营台账"}},{"id":"next","intent":"roadmap","items":3}]}
```

Supported intents: cover, conclusion, comparison, architecture, process, roadmap, kpi, decision, photo, screenshot, brand-sheet, trend, ranking, distribution and composition. `ready` means a supported baseline choice; `needs-evidence`, `split-required` and `custom-required` are real work to resolve before rendering. Keep the returned reasons in project notes, not as slide decoration.

The numeric renderer constraints are limits, not content targets. Do not fill all six slots just because a layout permits six items. Basic flow pages support up to four steps; native tables up to seven rows/six columns; charts up to eight labels/three series. Split by meaning before shrinking type.

## Selective knowledge layers

- Style: semantic palette, font roles, contrast and image language.
- Page purpose: opening, argument, comparison, evidence, conclusion.
- Composition: hierarchy, grid, grouping, density, whitespace.
- Visualization: data relationship and valid representation.
- Scenario: audience, decision and evidence requirements.
- Rules/evaluation: selection conditions, exclusions, measured failures and reviewed lessons.

These are classification facets, not six mandatory folders to load on every task. Eight style families are guidance; the bundled renderer currently has two concrete color themes. Do not claim eight fully designed theme implementations.

# Same-content evaluation

Compare a frozen baseline and proposed decision system on identical brief, facts, assets and output formats. Hold font availability and canvas size constant. Keep the old files intact. Compare the changed decisions and actual rendered pages, not two unrelated showcases.

## Hard gates

- No fabricated figures, quotes, customers or unsupported causal claims.
- No clipping, image distortion, dropped content or missing source labels.
- Real PPTX editability where promised; working H5 navigation/reading mode.
- Unknown data remains distinct from zero; fonts and page counts verified for PDF.

A hard-gate failure blocks promotion regardless of aesthetic score.

## Review dimensions

For each, record a concrete before/after observation and reviewer; optional 1–5 ratings are human judgments, not automated aesthetic proof.

1. Narrative: audience understands the conclusion and requested decision.
2. Hierarchy: one primary claim, evidence easy to locate, appropriate density.
3. Composition: alignment, whitespace, image intent and rhythm support meaning.
4. Data: correct representation, scale, unit, period, sources and missingness.
5. Consistency: stable brand, type roles and semantics across the deck.
6. Delivery: editable objects, H5 behavior and requested export quality.

Current repository tests cover ten design-decision scenarios plus portable export regression. They verify selection behavior, constraints and file properties, not that ten complete decks were visually accepted. Keep real output review separate. Only a reviewed reusable improvement enters shared rules; private project preferences remain local.

# Interaction lessons

Version: 2.1.0

Last updated: 2026-10-25

This ledger stores generalized methods only. It must not contain raw conversations, customer names, internal numbers, confidential strategy, or unlicensed source material.

## Narrative and content

- Understand the project, audience, and decision goal before designing the page sequence.
- Improve the argument instead of transferring a source deck page by page.
- Supplement thin content with logic, governance boundaries, evidence definitions, ownership, and actions; never fabricate business facts.

## Input handling

- Accept and inventory PDFs, PPTX files, images, logos, VI guides, screenshots, research, and structured data.
- When reusing a reference deck, create a brand replacement map and scan every output for old brand names, logos, filenames, and copied footer text.
- Preserve sources and usage rights for every externally sourced visual or factual claim.

## Visual hierarchy

- Prefer transparent-background logos.
- Place VI, products, scenarios, stores, packaging, screenshots, and evidence images in layouts that match their role.
- Use `contain` for screenshots, VI sheets, full products, packaging, and other assets whose complete silhouette matters.
- Use controlled `cover` only for documentary photography; record the subject focal point.
- Never enlarge weak imagery until it looks soft. Replace, reduce, or frame it.

## Typography and spacing

- Eliminate orphan characters, single-character lines, accidental title wrapping, meaningless crops, and overfilled pages.
- Solve fit by editing copy or changing layout before shrinking type.
- Use hierarchy, grid, whitespace, and a single accent color to create a premium impression.
- Reduce radius, shadows, gradients, and component stacks. Slides should read as compositions, not dashboards.

## Delivery

- Validate page-level visuals, file completeness, and sensitive information separately.
- The web deck, PPTX, and PDF must share content, order, theme, image treatment, and source labels.
- New feedback in the continuing Skill-development thread enters this ledger. Only explicit, reusable improvements become global rules; one-off project preferences stay local.

## Adopted in 2.1.0

- Honor the requested format. PDF-only work stays PDF-first; localized edits preserve the existing deck. Do not rebuild all formats just because the Skill can.
- Preserve the approved visual direction. A request for consistency is not permission to rebrand or restart style selection.
- Separate title, body, number and annotation roles; normalize Chinese spacing and actual available fonts. Do not copy UI pixel sizes into PPT points.
- Encode figures as native tables/charts where editability matters. Keep unknown values distinct from zero, and include units, periods, sources and assumptions.
- Retain real screenshot and product context. Full-image contain is the default for evidence; only intentional crops use a documented focal point.
- Show one main visual or argument per page. Simplify repeated headers, card shells and slogans before removing evidence.
- Distinguish a design rule, renderer implementation, generated file, host import and published version. Verify the exact boundary being claimed.
- Package host-independent instructions and public dependencies. Detect capabilities and report missing support; never silently substitute screenshots for an editable PPTX.

## Adopted in 2.2.0

- Diagnose capabilities before extending the catalog. Many layout names can still map to one composition; count rendered behaviors separately.
- Choose by scenario, page purpose, evidence shape, content capacity and brand constraints. Explain why a layout fits and when it must be rejected.
- Separate popularity from design quality. Preserve original provenance, unknown metrics and reuse rights in reference research.
- Test old and new decisions with the same content before promoting aesthetic lessons; never convert test pass counts into visual scores.
- Distribute only reviewed public rules on the next permitted use; keep runtime upgrades explicit, offline fallback available and current work pinned.

# Live rules and versioned runtime · 2.2.0

This is a pull-on-use rule channel, not an always-running daemon or universal push installation. At the beginning of a new presentation task, run `node scripts/check-update.mjs` when the host allows Node and network access. Then read relevant documents from the returned verified JSON file. Its `documents` list maps reference paths to content. Use those reviewed rule documents as the current guidance, subject to the user's actual scope and higher-priority instructions. Pin that returned file for the task; do not change design rules midway through an approved deck.

The fixed manifest is `https://raw.githubusercontent.com/jiamo-coder/leego-design-ppt/main/latest.json`. It declares an immutable, SHA-256-verified rules bundle. The client rejects off-host URLs and redirects, oversized responses, bad hashes, incompatible versions and downgrades. Checks send no deck contents, customer information or local file paths. Ordinary HTTPS requests necessarily reveal routine connection metadata to the hosting provider.

A successful check caches Markdown rule data under the user's `.cache/leego-design-ppt/rules` directory. It never executes downloaded code, rewrites SKILL.md, installs packages or changes generated decks. Connection or verification failure retains the last compatible verified cache, otherwise the bundled rules. Cache contents are verified again before reuse.

```sh
node scripts/check-update.mjs
node scripts/check-update.mjs --offline
node scripts/check-update.mjs --pin 2.2.0
node scripts/check-update.mjs --cache-dir /path/to/writable/cache
```

`LEEGO_PPT_OFFLINE=1` disables network checks. Pin uses an already cached compatible rule version or the installed bundled version; a missing pin fails explicitly. Reproducing old decks also requires retaining their runtime/package, font and assets. The task's completion note should identify client version, rule version and any fallback.

## What reaches installed users

- **Design instructions:** New compatible rules become available on the next task/check after a reviewed public release. Offline or restricted hosts continue their existing snapshot.
- **Scripts, dependencies, catalog formats and H5 runtime:** A new installable package is advertised. The recipient uses their host's supported upgrade/import flow; do not silently overwrite their software or preferences. Older clients cannot gain a new updater without a one-time package upgrade.
- **Already delivered presentations:** Stay unchanged. Regeneration or explicit edits are required to adopt later design choices.

An update in the maintainer's conversation is not a public release. Generalize and redact it, run relevant tests, publish immutable resources first and the manifest last. Unreviewed conversation text, client material and private feedback never enter the feed automatically. The publisher supports the current v1 rules protocol with `minClientVersion`; breaking capabilities require a new package. Existing 2.0/2.1 installations must upgrade once to 2.2+ for pull-on-use.

SHA-256 proves resource integrity against the HTTPS manifest, not independent author signing. Hosts with their own approvals, offline mode or custom-skill restrictions remain in control. Do not claim every existing user is instantly updated.

# Narrative and content optimization

## Communication job

Write one sentence before outlining:

`By the end, [audience] should [understand/believe/choose/approve/do] [outcome] because [central takeaway].`

For neutral or exploratory decks, define the questions the audience must be able to answer.

## Evidence-safe content model

Classify every statement:

- `verified`: supported by supplied material or a cited source;
- `inference`: a clearly labeled synthesis from verified material;
- `proposal`: recommended direction, action, or wording;
- `example`: illustrative and visibly marked as non-production data.

Never convert a proposal or example into a factual claim.

## Slide logic

Each slide requires:

- one narrative job;
- one audience-facing takeaway title;
- the minimum evidence needed to support it;
- one implication or transition.

Useful arcs include context -> stakes -> evidence -> implication -> action; question -> analysis -> answer; current state -> change -> future state; or problem -> causes -> recommendation.

## Editing rules

- Remove duplicate claims and repeated summaries.
- Replace topic titles such as “Market Analysis” with a specific takeaway.
- Prefer concrete verbs and audience language over abstract noun clusters.
- Keep production notes and model instructions out of visible copy.
- End on a decision, action, synthesis, or useful question, not a generic thanks page.

# PPTX and PDF generation · 2.1.0

Use the public Node.js/PptxGenJS exporter included in the Skill. `npm ci --ignore-scripts` installs locked dependencies; it is a one-time host setup, not part of each build. Run `doctor.mjs` when the environment is unknown. Do not assume `@oai/artifact-tool` or host-private module paths exist.

`build-pptx.mjs` and `build-web.mjs` share `scene.mjs` for content, geometry, theme and estimated text bounds. They preserve ordinary text and shapes, PNG/JPEG images with contain or focal cover, native tables, and bar/line charts. A `*.report.json` file records requested font and the scene; it is structural evidence, not visual acceptance. The narrative catalog is broader than the helper's baseline compositions. Custom compositions should retain the same QA rules rather than force-fitting content to a generic grid.

Use `table: {columns: [...], rows: [[...]]}` or `chart: {type: "bar"|"line", unit, period, labels: [...], series: [{name, values: [...]}]}`. Charts require sources. Complex charts, missing-value gaps and long tables need deliberate custom authoring or pagination. The helper rejects unsupported mixed content instead of silently omitting it.

## PDF from final PPTX

Run `export-pdf.mjs` with LibreOffice or export the final PPTX in PowerPoint/WPS. A private temporary conversion directory isolates the export from other open documents and avoids accepting a stale PDF. Reopen the PDF and check page count, text, image crop and fonts. Different office renderers may vary; record the exporter.

The older `build-pdf.py` remains available for an explicitly requested image-based, pixel-stable PDF from final rendered PNG pages. This produces raster PDF pages, not selectable/editable content. Do not confuse it with native PDF export.

Only deliver requested formats. For PDF-only work a temporary PPTX is implementation detail. If a converter is missing, deliver the available authorized output and report the precise missing capability. Do not claim HTML printing proves PowerPoint fidelity.

If a headless converter substitutes fonts or renders Chinese as boxes, pass `--font-dir "/path/to/licensed/fonts"` to export-pdf.mjs. This sets a temporary fontconfig for that export only. Re-render and inspect actual glyphs; a zero exit status is not proof of usable Chinese text. The directory is not copied into the Skill.

# Presenter notes and sources

Speaker notes should help delivery without leaking production instructions.

For each slide, store:

- purpose;
- 2-4 talking points;
- transition to the next slide;
- timing only when requested;
- citations and asset attributions.

Use a machine-readable source block when external sources are used:

```xml
<sources>
- https://example.com/source-page
</sources>
```

Keep a small human-readable source label on the slide when the audience needs it. Never expose internal file paths, search IDs, tool tokens, or uncited copied claims.

# QA, release, and versioning

## Validation layers

1. Semantic: required fields, valid layout IDs, evidence labels, and replacements.
2. Visual: page-by-page render review, typography, whitespace, crop, resolution, contrast.
3. File: openability, page count, ordering, editable PPTX objects, links, and metadata.
4. Safety: banned terms, brand residue, private names, internal data, unlicensed assets, and secrets.

## Required checks (automatic plus manual)

- invalid or missing `deck-spec` fields;
- unresolved placeholders and TODO markers;
- banned brand terms in JSON, HTML, notes, and extracted PDF/PPTX text;
- single-character lines and accidental title wrapping;
- low-resolution images or missing files;
- PPTX layout overflow and overlap indicators;
- HTML broken assets and external runtime dependencies;
- PDF/PPTX page-count mismatch;
- manifest hashes and resource URLs.

The included scripts cover schema, supported content, basic geometry and text/asset checks. They do not automatically prove visual quality, office-suite fidelity, PDF font correctness, every link, or every item above. Inspect rendered pages and extracted file structures separately. Record the actual host, version, font, tested formats and untested platforms; importing a Skill does not prove the host agent can generate every format.

## Release order

1. Validate Skill, scripts, templates, and anonymized examples.
2. Build website, sample HTML/PPTX/PDF, and downloadable Skill ZIP.
3. Calculate SHA-256 for every released resource.
4. Publish resources first.
5. Publish `latest.json` last.
6. Confirm website fallback and remote manifest behavior.

## Versioning

- Patch: typography, copy, QA, and compatibility fixes.
- Minor: new theme, layout, output capability, or formal workflow.
- Major: incompatible `deck-spec` or runtime change.

The Skill does not silently self-update. Remote rules are accepted only from the fixed HTTPS host and only after hash verification.

# Reference collection and promotion

Collect external examples only when that research is requested. Diagnose the current Skill first; a large image folder is not a design knowledge base. Start with a manageable, diverse sample (30–50 candidates is a future research target, not a quota or completed library).

## Candidate record

Record stable id, platform, original page URL, creator, observed date, page purpose, scenario, style family, grid/hierarchy, palette, typography, density, reusable rule, exclusions, asset rights, evidence and review status. Keep likes/saves/comments separate with observation time and access status. Unknown counts are null, never zero or an invented rank. A thumbnail proxy is not the original author page or a verified platform statistic.

Use `data/reference-cases.json` for reviewed public records. It starts empty intentionally. Source image collection is optional; keep licensed assets or reference links, not copied paid template packs. Do not access private material, bypass platform restrictions or package client source decks. User-provided historical discussions are strategy proposals until independently verified; do not describe their references as freshly inspected.

## Two independent assessments

Platform popularity helps discover candidates; it does not establish professional quality. Evaluate design quality through evidence clarity, hierarchy, readability, brand fit, editing feasibility and accessibility. A social cover can be effective marketing yet unsuitable for a shareholder report.

Promotion requires a verified source (or an explicitly original synthetic case), a concrete extracted principle, applicable conditions, counterexamples, rights notes and a same-content test. States: candidate → inspected → rule-proposed → benchmarked → approved/rejected. Never promote by popularity alone. Record reviewer/date and failed cases; omit unsupported scores rather than manufacture precision.

A reusable lesson states: “When [content and audience conditions], use [composition] because [observable benefit]; avoid when [countercondition].” Copying appearance without those conditions is not a learned rule.

# Web presentations · 2.1.0

The Node-only builder copies local assets and produces an offline `index.html` with CSS/JS beside it. No CDN, account, remote image or external font request is added. Paths with spaces and Chinese names are supported.

Desktop presentation mode uses a fixed 1280 × 720 scene scaled to the viewport. Reading mode reflows text and images; mobile starts in reading mode. Tables preserve column relationships through a horizontally scrollable region. Controls: arrows/PageUp/PageDown for slides, O for overview, N for notes, R for reading. Overview shows all pages and clicking a page returns to presentation. Do not claim audience-window synchronization: this version does not implement it.

Keyboard navigation ignores input/editable controls. Storage is per deck and guarded against file-origin restrictions. Touch swipes navigate only in presentation mode, not during vertical reading. No global wheel interception, autoplay or animated number counting. Reduced-motion has a static result.

Check desktop and 390/320 px reading, long titles, table overflow, images, keyboard and overview. A CSS preference or successful build is not a browser test. The included print CSS targets presentation mode; PDF parity is verified by exporting the PPTX instead.

# Typography and layout · 2.1.0

## Geometry and units

Default presentation canvas: 1280 × 720 CSS px, 16:9; safe margins 72 px horizontal and 56–64 px vertical. Use an 8 px spacing rhythm and 24–32 px gutters as starting values, not a requirement to rebuild a supplied template.

The native exporter uses 13⅓ × 7½ inches: divide canvas coordinates by 96, and multiply pixel font sizes by 0.75 for points. Do not mix UI px, PPT pt, or native app dp/sp.

| Role | Canvas px | Approximate PPT pt |
|---|---:|---:|
| Cover | 58–72 | 43.5–54 |
| Slide title | 40–48 | 30–36 |
| Key metric | 40–64 | 30–48 |
| Subhead | 26–32 | 19.5–24 |
| Body | 24–30 | 18–22.5 |
| Source note | 14–18 | 10.5–13.5 |

These are ranges, not universal minimums for inherited decks. Check projected readability. The baseline exporter may use smaller supporting copy; revise for audience and viewing distance.

## Typeface and weights

Use MiSans for new Leego-family work when legally available on the render/view host. Body Regular 400, subheads Medium 500, titles/key metrics Semibold 600. Preserve protected brand lettering. Chinese character spacing is zero; never compress glyphs or apply negative tracking to fit copy. Keep original font files out of a distributable Skill.

PPTX regular/bold does not guarantee Medium/Semibold faces or font embedding. Confirm the real rendered face. If MiSans is missing, choose an available CJK family such as Source Han Sans SC or Microsoft YaHei via `style.fontFace`, state the fallback, and inspect actual wrapping. Do not label font unification complete based on a CSS name alone.

## Fit and rhythm

- Retain a common title axis, picture captions and source placement across the deck.
- Keep meaning intact: edit redundancy, widen the right region, change composition or split the page before shrinking text.
- Intentional two-line headlines are acceptable; single-character tails, clipped titles and accidental three-line headings are not.
- Alternate evidence-heavy and synthesis pages. Do not turn every page into three cards or repeat a dashboard shell.
- Preserve content that carries the object, period, unit, denominator, risk or decision. Remove repeated labels and decorative wrappers first.
- Preserve complete UI screenshots, VI sheets and product silhouettes. A detail crop must retain a context view or clearly identify the crop.

Use a restrained accent and whitespace to establish hierarchy. Semantic risk colors are separate from brand color. Motion must have a static equivalent and respect reduced-motion; do not animate numbers from zero as if they were measured progress.

# Translating Leego UI into presentation standards

Derived from Leego Design UI 2.29.4 and completed presentation iterations, reviewed 2026-10-25. The other Skill is not a runtime dependency.

| Source principle | Presentation rule | Do not import |
|---|---|---|
| MiSans semantic hierarchy | Use available licensed family, 400/500/600 hierarchy, zero Chinese tracking; verify real output | UI 14 px body size as a projected slide standard |
| Stable icon identity and optical sizing | Reuse supplied approved SVG/PNG assets, one semantic family and visually equal slots; use static portable images | Private icon service access, remote scripts, full icon-library copies |
| Data semantics | Same metric keeps name, unit, period, source, denominator and risk meaning across slides | Fake health scores, null→0 conversions, illustrative values as business results |
| Content-driven tables | Keep necessary columns, meaningful order, readable native table and consistent padding; split by row/column groups | Sticky web columns, pagination controls and 20 px as a universal PPT rule |
| Progressive disclosure | Put primary conclusion and evidence on the slide; detail in notes/appendix or a clearly labeled companion demo | Hover-only evidence or essential content visible only during animation |
| Remove repeated containers | One page task, clear main visual, fewer wrappers and repeated headers | Dashboard card walls, login dialogs, sidebars and business form controls |
| Separate state and evidence | Distinguish concept, prototype, local test, published artifact and operational result | Calling a screenshot real integration or an exported file accepted by the recipient |

## Data pictures

Choose a chart for the question: bars for magnitude/rank, lines for time, matrices for comparison, flows for movement, trees for hierarchy. No decorative globe without geographic meaning. Bar charts include a zero baseline; explicitly identify any different scale. Mark units, periods, scope, missingness and source. When values are unknown, preserve that state; do not draw zero. The included basic chart engine rejects missing values; use a custom chart with gaps when needed.

Keep explanatory tables and charts native/editable in PPTX. A screenshot of a real UI remains an image: do not label it an editable dashboard. If SVG is used, verify compatibility or provide a PNG fallback without claiming vector editability.

## Public learning boundary

Publish generalized decisions and synthetic examples. Do not package customer decks, source screenshots, private names, internal numbers, font binaries or client-specific approvals. A project-specific theme, page count, legal clause or decorative choice does not become a universal style rule.
